URL: https://som3aware.pages.dev/#/work/cypienta

Cypienta
Security data platform that condenses and contextualizes telemetry before it reaches SIEM, SOAR and AI tools.

role: design system · interfaces
where: Cypienta · 2026–
stack: Svelte · Django
highlight: company-wide design system, in progress
about
Security teams are flooded with events, logs and alerts. Cypienta groups and condenses that telemetry, so SIEM, SOAR and AI tools get context instead of noise.
what I did

- revamping the app interfaces (in progress)
- building a unified design system for the company (in progress)
- polishing the marketing sites, which the company built
- some backend work

Stayro
Guest and host rental apps for the Saudi marketplace.

role: team lead · mobile · infra
where: Eignspaces · 2025–26
stack: React Native · Expo · EAS · GitHub Actions · GCP · Redis · Celery
highlight: to the App Store in ~3 months
about
Guests and hosts in Saudi Arabia needed rental apps that meet local requirements, like national identity, Ministry of Tourism compliance and local payments, on a two-to-three-month release schedule.
what I did

- guided a junior developer through the Nafath national identity integration with docs and support
- fixed bugs and got key flows working, including payments and the Ministry of Tourism flow
- set up and managed GCP: Cloud Run, Cloud SQL and Redis for an async Celery backend
- owned CI/CD with GitHub Actions and EAS, building and publishing to the App Store
- worked with the UI/UX designer to improve screens and flows

## work / This portfolio

This portfolio

where: side project · 2026
stack: React · TypeScript · Tailwind CSS · Vite · Vitest · Cloudflare Pages
highlight: ~90 themes · keyboard-first
about

## about

URL: https://som3aware.pages.dev/#/about

About
I started out designing posters for university clubs and never stopped. Now I build the whole product behind the interface too: web, mobile, and the design systems that hold them together.
I'm Ahmed Abu Qahf (som3aware), a full-stack engineer in Tanta, Egypt, working remotely. I work in the space between design and engineering: interfaces, the design systems behind them, and the products around them, on web and mobile.
journey

early: My fascination with computers started on visits to the countryside, rushing to use my cousin's computer, the first in our family, to explore apps and the early internet.
6th grade: Ranked top of my whole governorate and got my first laptop as the prize.
prep school: Moved from using computers to managing them, installing operating systems, and wrote my first code in Visual Basic.NET: calculators and tools for the area and circumference of shapes.
2013: Won 2nd place nationwide in JICA's first essay competition in Egypt, run with the Ministry of Education and sponsored by Toshiba El Araby, writing about my dreams for the future. Out of about 1,000 essays.
2014–19: Studied computer engineering at AUC on a scholarship. Designed flyers and posters for student clubs (SPE, the Society of Petroleum Engineers; Glow; CSTA, the Community of Scientific and Technological Activities) and for yoga instructor sessions: my first design work.
2018: Intern on Vodafone's meeting-room booking app: designed most of the screens and built the back end.
2018–19: Hackathons: Hajj Hackathon in Jeddah (Kun 3awnan, IoT help for pilgrims) and Dell EMC 423x.
2020–21: First full-time job at VOIS. Within months, sole maintainer of a COVID-19 mobility platform for governments, working with a UK supervisor. Helped rescue a late HR system and built a React Native component library from Vodafone's brand guidelines.
2021–23: New Smart Egypt: software for government, enterprise and public places. An agricultural delivery-tracking app, the Ramses Station free Wi-Fi journey (designed and built), fingerprint-scanner integrations with Odoo. Deployed on cloud and on-premise.
2022–23: MSE in Software Engineering at ASU, online, while working full time. 4.0 GPA, including a master's class on mobile systems with React Native.
2023: Nodogoro: moved into AI products. Led Outlined AI and built LLM tools.
2024–26: Eignspaces: client product work. Reconciled (acquired by LaborEdge), Hivo and Stayro.
2026–: Cypienta: a company-wide design system and an interface revamp for a security data platform.
education

2022–23: MSE, Software Engineering · Arizona State University · 4.0 / 4.0 GPA · AGFE OLS scholarship
2014–19: BSc, Computer Engineering · The American University in Cairo · Egyptian Public Schools scholarship
awards: 2nd place nationwide, JICA essay competition (first edition) (2013)
courses: Forward Program, McKinsey & Company (2024) · React Development Cross-Skilling Nanodegree, Udacity (2022) · Advanced Full-Stack Web Development Nanodegree, Udacity (2022)
hackathons: Hajj Hackathon, Jeddah (2018) · Dell EMC 423x Hackathon, New Cairo (2019) · NodoAI (company hackathon), Nodogoro (2023)
outside work

family: Family first. Loving husband, and I love kids.
talk: I love reading, discussing and talking about history, football, tech and programming. I watch a lot of history too.
football: Played football until preparatory school. Still watch it, and play FIFA.
code for fun: I like using programming for genuine, personal things, like the site I made for my wife's birthday. happy-birthday-rody.pages.dev ↗
drawing: I used to draw, and still do from time to time.
saxophone: Used to take saxophone lessons from my aunt's husband.
writing: Product decisions and lessons from shipping, on Hashnode. som3aware.hashnode.dev ↗
life: Recently married, so learning that renovating an apartment is a very different kind of engineering.

## philosophy

URL: https://som3aware.pages.dev/#/philosophy

Philosophy
The values I live and work by, each one backed by the work.

- 01 Honest and straightforward
I value people who are genuine and say what they mean, and I try to be one: no spin, no detours, just what I did and what I didn't.
in practice: Every number on this site has a source, and shared work says so.
- 02 Open mind, patient ear
I try to hear the whole story before forming a view, and to stay patient while I do.
in practice: Tracing a months-old map bug at VOIS to its real cause, a platform setting, instead of the obvious suspect.
- 03 Keep it simple
I like taking complex things and making them simple, at work and at home. If it can be easier to use, I'll make it easier.
in practice: A Wi-Fi portal cut to a few clear steps; one view for invoice matching at Reconciled.
- 04 Small details, big impact
I notice the small stuff, the spacing, the empty state, the button that feels off, because that's what people feel.
in practice: This site's themes and keyboard states; screens refined with designers on Hivo and Stayro.
- 05 Creative, but realistic
I like creative ideas that can actually ship. Not everything fits the budget, the timeline or the team, so I look for the version that does.
in practice: Shipping Stayro's guest and host apps in two to three months; at Reconciled, “balance creativity with practical execution” (Brock Rumer).
- 06 Keep learning
I'm always eager to learn and grow, to be a better version of myself than I was yesterday.
in practice: An MSE at ASU while working full time; moving from web to mobile, AI and now design systems.
- 07 Help people grow
Helping someone get unstuck is my favourite part of the job. I mentor junior engineers and interns, and show teams how to use AI well.
in practice: Mentored interns and juniors on Hivo and Reconciled; led and reviewed a team of two; guided a junior through the Nafath integration.
- 08 Share what I know
